focus: Actual trainable QNNs and quantum circuit attention; classical memory is no longer the main study.
useful_observations: Shared post-encoding unitaries are untrainable for fidelity attention; observed cancellation ~1e-15.
Consistently scaling re-uploaded inputs improves trained-head test accuracy from 85.16% in the initial study to 95.55% on new test data; different cohorts, not a paired treatment estimate.
Adaptive sparse readout improves finite-shot retrieval and weighted-value error in toy attention; strong classical metric still wins.

weighted_values.limitation: Sparse and dense heads differ semantically. Calibration costs 819200 validation shots/seed/method; not an end-to-end resource gain.

next_experiments: Inspect AQKA and QASA full methods/code; adaptive shot allocation and parameter placement are not presumed novel.
Vary candidate count, input domain, training seeds and realistic noise correlations; charge adaptive-round latency.
Compare output-vector estimation against sparse and dense classical/quantum controls on identical tasks.
Only then integrate head into a small complete hybrid transformer with capacity-matched controls.
checks: Soft-value output evaluated, not only winning key
Adaptive API extension preserves earlier behavior
hardware: None; do not submit without separate authorization.
